name: Shunt and power entry
question: Which shunt, and how should the power entry move right?
why_now:
D12-5 (C): a bigger 4-terminal shunt, or two 0.5 mΩ in parallel if none is found. D12-4 (B): move the power entry right so the VBAT_PROT planes are fed nearer mid-board, spread out for the via fields. The shunt's footprint shapes the power entry's layout, so the two are decided together; the layout itself then comes to you as a block page.

All of the node's current, up to 60 A, passes the shunt. The LM74910H breaker and short-circuit threshold and the INA228 range are set from its value (DEC-001, DEC-002).

facts.label: Search
facts.value: 15 parts compared (Isabellenhütte BVR, BVB; Vishay WSLP4026, WSK1216; Stackpole HCSK4026, CSS; KOA PSG4; Bourns CSS4J; and others), live DigiKey/Mouser data and datasheets, 2026-11-03. 1216-size parts rejected: their force lands can't take a 60 A via field

facts.label: Best 4-terminal part
facts.value: Isabellenhütte BVR-Z, 4026 body (10.1 × 6.6 mm): ZERANIN alloy, TCR 0 ± 20 ppm/K (today ±50), AEC-Q200, −65…+170 °C, separate Kelvin leads, force lands 2.55 × 5.6 mm with a 5.5 mm gap. No 0.25 mΩ code. DigiKey only (Mouser doesn't list it); the second source is Vishay WSLP4026 (same outline, other land pattern, ±75 ppm/K)

facts.label: Derating at 125 °C
facts.value: At an estimated 145 °C terminal temperature: R0003 5 W available for 1.08 W at 60 A (3.1×); R0002 6 W for 0.72 W (5.6×); R0005 3.1 W for 0.45 W at 30 A (4.6×). The handbook asks for 1.5×

facts.label: Library
facts.value: BVR-Z-R0002-1.0 and BVR-Z-R0003-1.0 and the R_Shunt_Isabellenhuette_BVR4026 footprint are already in the library; R0005 needs a symbol. The library's 3D model is 2.4 mm tall where DigiKey gives 3.45–3.80 mm: to be corrected (still far under the 6.17 mm limit)

facts.label: Today's 60 A path
facts.value: J910 (x 102 mm) → east to Q201/Q202 (x 126–146) → back west through R201 (x 116) → Q203/Q204 (x 95–106) → VBAT_PROT: about 74 mm of 60 A copper, and the planes are fed at the west end (x ≈ 99)

options.name: BVR-Z-R0003-1.0, 0.3 mΩ
options.summary: R208 (ILIM) 32 k → 26.7 kΩ for a 74.8 A breaker; R210 (RISCP) 0 Ω → 383 Ω, which keeps today's short-circuit window exactly (80 A typical, 71.4–92 A). INA228 ADCRANGE 1 stays; CURRENT_LSB 260.4 µA, SHUNT_CAL 4096.
costs: Two resistor values and DEC-001/002 updated

options.name: BVR-Z-R0002-1.0, 0.2 mΩ
options.summary: R208 → 40.2 kΩ for 74.5 A; R210 stays 0 Ω, so the short-circuit trip rises to 100 A typical (89–115 A) and can't be set lower.
costs: Short-circuit trip 25 % higher; the FETs' SOA at 115 A has to be checked

options.name: 2 × BVR-Z-R0005-1.0 in parallel (the fallback)
options.summary: 0.25 mΩ effective, so every setting stays. The INA228 averages the two through matched 0.1 % resistors (2 × 20 Ω per input); the LM74910H senses one shunt and relies on an even split.

measures.label: Short-circuit trip
measures.value: as today, if the copper splits evenly (0.05 mΩ of asymmetry = +4.8 %)

measures.label: Settings changed
measures.value: none; 4 averaging resistors and a new library symbol

costs: The breaker's accuracy depends on mirror-symmetric copper

recommendation.why: A bigger 4-terminal shunt exists, so D12-5's first choice holds; 0.3 mΩ keeps today's short-circuit protection exactly with one added resistor, where 0.2 mΩ would raise it 25 %.

decisions.question: How should the power entry move right?
decisions.why_now: The 60 A path costs about 0.007 mΩ per mm on four layers (the pre-protection nets get In2/In3 in the power-entry region, where the VBAT_PROT planes are cut back), so path length is loss: about 0.24 W per 10 mm at 60 A. Figures below are estimates from that rate; the block page will model the real layout.

options.name: Shift the group east as it is
options.summary: Every part moves about 35 mm east, keeping today's order and spacing (spread a little for the vias).

measures.label: Loss in the 60 A path at 60 A

costs: The run from J910 grows by the shift: about 0.9 W more loss for 0.1 mΩ of balance

options.name: Re-order it to flow east
options.summary: Same parts, same block, the chain laid in the current's order: Q201/Q202 beside J910, then the shunt, then Q203/Q204 at about x 142, U201/U202 beside the shunt, spread for the via fields. It ends about 43 mm further east than today.

measures.label: Loss in the 60 A path at 60 A

gains: Shorter 60 A path and the feed moved right: lower DCR and better balance at once
costs: The group is rearranged, not just shifted: a new block page replaces D04

options.name: Compact at J910
options.summary: Everything packed as close to J910 as the via fields allow; the planes are fed at the west end.

measures.label: Loss in the 60 A path at 60 A

costs: The supply imbalance stays (you chose D12-4 B to reduce it)

recommendation.why: It is what D12-4 B asks for done the efficient way: the feed moves right and the 60 A path gets shorter instead of longer. A plain shift pays about 0.9 W for 0.1 mΩ of balance.

answer: Reply with each decision and a letter, for example "D14-1 A, D14-2 B", or a change.
sources: shunt search report (2026-11-03): Isabellenhütte BVR/BVB datasheets, Vishay WSLP4026 doc 30180, Stackpole SEI-HCSK, DigiKey/Mouser APIs
